items.title: Push and deploy
items.body:
STEP 1 — Install Git (if you haven't).
  Open the terminal (Anaconda Prompt on Win, Terminal on Mac).
  Type: git --version
  If you see 'command not found', install Git from https://git-scm.com

STEP 2 — Push to GitHub.
  Open the 'create new repository' card above. Name: beanforge. Public. Create.
  In your terminal:
      cd Desktop/beanforge
      git init
      git add .
      git commit -m "Bean Forge cafe site v0.1"
      git branch -M main
      git remote add origin https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/beanforge.git
      git push -u origin main

STEP 3 — Deploy on Netlify.
  Open the Netlify sign up card. Sign up with your GitHub account (easiest).
  In the dashboard, click 'Add new site' → 'Import an existing project' → GitHub → pick the 'beanforge' repo → click 'Deploy'.
  After about 30 seconds you get a URL like 'unusual-cookie-1234.netlify.app'.
  YOU SHOULD SEE: your Bean Forge site live at that URL.

STEP 4 — Rename the URL.
  In Netlify, go to Site settings → Domain management → click the random subdomain → change to 'yourname-beanforge'.
  New URL: yourname-beanforge.netlify.app

  Open the URL on your phone. Tap the phone link. Tap the address. Everything should work.

items.title: Final polish
items.body:
STEP 1 — Add a favicon (the tiny icon in browser tabs).
  Go to https://favicon.io/emoji-favicons/hot-beverage and download.
  Unzip the file. Move the 'favicon.ico' into your beanforge folder.
  In index.html <head>, add: <link rel='icon' href='favicon.ico'>

STEP 2 — Add Open Graph tags (for nice WhatsApp / Twitter previews).
  In <head>, add:
      <meta name='description' content='Bean Forge — Coffee, sharpened.'>
      <meta property='og:title' content='Bean Forge'>
      <meta property='og:description' content='Specialty coffee, sharpened.'>

STEP 3 — Run Lighthouse.
  In Chrome on your live Netlify URL, press F12 → 'Lighthouse' tab → click 'Analyze page load'.
  YOU SHOULD SEE: scores for Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices, SEO. Aim for 90+ on all.
  Take a screenshot. Save as 'lighthouse.png' in your folder.

STEP 4 — Write README.md.
  In VS Code, new file: README.md. Type:

      # Bean Forge
      A 1-page site for a fictional specialty coffee shop.
      
      ## Live URL
      https://yourname-beanforge.netlify.app
      
      ## Tech
      Plain HTML + CSS. No framework. Deployed on Netlify.
      
      ## Lighthouse
      ![Lighthouse scores](lighthouse.png)

STEP 5 — Push everything.
      git add .
      git commit -m "Add favicon, OG tags, Lighthouse, README"
      git push

  Netlify auto-redeploys in 30 seconds.

PASS CRITERIA — Bean Forge v0.1 ships when:
  ☐ Live URL works on phone and desktop
  ☐ Phone number is tappable on mobile
  ☐ Map link opens Google Maps
  ☐ Lighthouse 90+ on all 4 categories
  ☐ README has the live URL at the top
  ☐ Favicon shows in the browser tab

weeks.title: Security — The Threats You Haven't Thought About
weeks.context: Most web apps leak data through obvious holes — SQL injection that Prisma prevents, XSS that React mostly prevents, CSRF that SameSite cookies mostly prevent. The non-obvious ones are what get you. This week you audit your URL shortener against the OWASP Top 10 and fix every issue.

Authentication and session attacks — fixation, hijacking, brute force
Authorisation bugs — IDOR (insecure direct object references), the most common bug class
Secrets in code — git history scanning, secret rotation
Dependency vulnerabilities — npm audit, Snyk, Dependabot
tasks: Run `npm audit` and `snyk test` on your URL shortener; fix the high/critical issues

weeks.title: Scaling — When 10x More Traffic Hits
weeks.context: Most apps never need to scale. The ones that do are usually broken by an N+1 query or a missing index, not by needing distributed systems. This week you stress-test your URL shortener and fix the bottlenecks before they exist in production.

Stateless servers — why your servers should be cattle, not pets
Bottleneck order — CPU, memory, network, disk, database — usually database
